chunks: My father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali al-Jahdhami, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Becoming sorry is sufficient as repentance.
ai.seo_question: What is the role of regret in Islamic repentance according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this concise maxim from Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), highlighting that genuine internal remorse (*nadam*) is not merely a precursor to repentance but is itself sufficient to constitute *tawbah*. This hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on the sincerity of the heart, suggesting that true regret inherently motivates the cessation of sin and the resolve to return to God, thereby fulfilling the spiritual essence of repentance without requiring elaborate external rituals.
